data.name: Description
data.value: Review devices you can safely disable, interrupt settings, the USB path of your input devices and tweaks that hurt stability. Every change asks for confirmation and can be undone.

data.name: Scanned
data.value: Scanned at {0}. Nothing is changed until you choose an action.

data.name: ScanFailed
data.value: The scan could not be completed: {0}

data.name: DevicesDescription
data.value: Plug and Play inventory with notes on devices that latency guides often disable, and what stops working if you do. "Not present" or "no children" never proves a device is unused.

data.name: EnableAllHint
data.value: Re-enables every device that TweakHub disabled. Devices disabled elsewhere are left as they are.

data.name: DisableConfirmMessage
data.value: {0} will be disabled in Device Manager. You can enable it again from this list or with Re-enable all.

data.name: HighRiskWarning
data.value: Warning: this is a core system, storage, network or input device. Disabling it can stop Windows from booting or leave you without keyboard, mouse or network.

data.name: AvoidWarning
data.value: This device is often listed in latency guides, but disabling it gives no reliable benefit and can cause problems. TweakHub recommends leaving it enabled.

data.name: InterruptsDescription
data.value: PCI devices and how they signal the CPU. MSI (message signaled interrupts) avoids shared interrupt lines; priority and CPU affinity are advanced settings that only help in specific cases.

data.name: EditorHint
data.value: Change only what you need, one device at a time, and test after the restart. Restore original puts back the values TweakHub found.

data.name: MsiNotSupported
data.value: The driver of this device does not declare MSI support.

data.name: AffinityHint
data.value: Select the CPUs that may handle this device's interrupts. Leave all off to keep the current setting; use Restore original to go back to automatic.

data.name: ApplyConfirmMessage
data.value: TweakHub will back up and change the interrupt settings of {0}. If the device stops working after the restart, use Restore original or Safe Mode.

data.name: ApplyFailedMessage
data.value: The change could not be written or verified. Check that you accepted the administrator prompt.

data.name: UsbDescription
data.value: The path from each mouse, keyboard and controller to the CPU: every external hub adds a hop, and USB power saving can add wake-up delays.

data.name: PlanSuspendDescription
data.value: Lets Windows power down idle USB devices in the active plan. Turning it off avoids wake-up spikes on desktops; laptops may lose some battery life.

data.name: PlanSuspendOn
data.value: Enabled in the active plan (on AC power)

data.name: PlanSuspendOff
data.value: Disabled in the active plan (on AC power)

data.name: PlanSuspendUnknown
data.value: Not available in the active plan

data.name: PollingDescription
data.value: Estimates how often your mouse reports to Windows from raw input messages. Browser-free and local; for microsecond precision use DeepPoll.

data.name: PollingMove
data.value: Move the mouse quickly in circles for 4 seconds…

data.name: PollingTooFew
data.value: Not enough movement was captured. Keep TweakHub focused and move the mouse continuously.

data.name: PollingResult
data.value: {0} reports measured. The bars show how stable the rate was.

data.name: NoInputDevices
data.value: No mouse, keyboard or controller was found.

data.name: HubsNone
data.value: Direct to the controller (no external hubs)

data.name: ReconnectNote
data.value: Done. Unplug and reconnect the device, or restart, to apply the change.

data.name: ChecksDescription
data.value: Looks for popular tweaks that hurt stability, security or input (the RepairBadTweaks list) and puts the Windows default back. Registry repairs keep a backup and can be undone.

data.name: ChecksScanElevatedHint
data.value: Also reads boot timer settings, which need administrator rights.

data.name: ChecksManagedNote
data.value: Win32PrioritySeparation, Prefetch and SysMain are managed by Registry Tweaks, where TweakHub keeps their backups.

data.name: RepairConfirmMessage
data.value: {0} will be set back to the Windows default.

data.name: RepairNoUndo
data.value: This repair runs a Windows command and cannot be undone from TweakHub.

data.name: RepairVerifyFailed
data.value: The registry change could not be verified.

data.name: CheckStatusNeedsAdministrator
data.value: Check as administrator to read this

data.name: CategoryHealthyHint
data.value: Present and without Plug and Play problems. This does not measure how much it is used.

data.name: CategoryNotPresentHint
data.value: Remembered by Windows but not connected now. Not a reason to remove it.

data.name: CategoryProblemHint
data.value: Windows reports an error for this device: diagnose the driver instead of disabling it.

data.name: CategoryIdleBusHint
data.value: A bus or enumerator with no devices attached right now; it may be needed when a device appears later.

data.name: RuleHpet
data.value: High precision event timer: often disabled in latency guides, but modern Windows chooses its timers itself and turning it off brings no reliable gain.

data.name: RuleHpetBreaks
data.value: Some games, tools and older drivers that expect it; timing can become less stable.

data.name: RuleSmBus
data.value: SMBus controller: reads memory and sensor chips on the motherboard.

data.name: RuleSmBusBreaks
data.value: Hardware monitoring, RAM information, RGB lighting and fan control tools.

data.name: RuleKernelDebug
data.value: Network adapter used only for kernel debugging over the network.

data.name: RuleSystemSpeaker
data.value: Motherboard beeper for old-style system beeps.

data.name: RuleWanMiniport
data.value: Built-in VPN and dial-up protocols (IKEv2, L2TP, PPTP, SSTP, PPPoE).

data.name: RuleWanMiniportBreaks
data.value: Windows VPN connections, PPPoE internet and some third-party VPN clients.

data.name: RuleRdpBus
data.value: Redirects local devices into Remote Desktop sessions.

data.name: RuleRdpBusBreaks
data.value: Printers, drives and USB devices inside Remote Desktop sessions.

data.name: RuleVirtualDrive
data.value: Creates the virtual disks Windows mounts from VHD and VHDX files.

data.name: RuleVirtualDriveBreaks
data.value: Mounting virtual disks (VHD/VHDX) and tools that rely on them.

data.name: RuleNdisVirtual
data.value: Creates virtual network adapters for VPNs and virtualization tools.

data.name: RuleNdisVirtualBreaks
data.value: Some VPN clients and virtual machine networking.

data.name: RuleUmBusBreaks
data.value: Some sensors, portable devices, printers and mixed reality headsets.

data.name: RuleCompositeBus
data.value: Bus Windows uses to build composite devices.

data.name: RuleCompositeBusBreaks
data.value: Some wireless adapters, Bluetooth LE devices and docking stations.

data.name: RuleHyperVBreaks
data.value: Hyper-V, WSL 2, Windows Sandbox, Docker Desktop and virtualization-based security.

data.name: RuleWifiDirect
data.value: Virtual adapter for Wi-Fi Direct connections.

data.name: RuleWifiDirectBreaks
data.value: Mobile hotspot, wireless display (Miracast) and nearby sharing over Wi-Fi.

data.name: RuleTeredoBreaks
data.value: Xbox network party chat and multiplayer on some networks, and older IPv6 setups.

data.name: RuleVirtualPrinter
data.value: Virtual printer queue (PDF, XPS, Fax or OneNote).

data.name: CheckBcdTimersExplain
data.value: useplatformclock, disabledynamictick, useplatformtick and tscsyncpolicy are meant for debugging; forcing them usually increases timer overhead.

data.name: CheckMitigationsExplain
data.value: FeatureSettingsOverride turns off Spectre and Meltdown protections. The speed gain on current CPUs is small and the PC becomes exploitable.

data.name: CheckAutoTuningExplain
data.value: Restricting auto-tuning limits download speed on fast connections and does not lower ping.

data.name: CheckSvcHostSplitExplain
data.value: Raising SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB only hides processes in Task Manager; separate service hosts are more stable.

data.name: CheckThreadDpcExplain
data.value: ThreadDpcEnable=0 forces all deferred procedure calls to run at high priority, which can make latency worse.

data.name: CheckErrorReportingExplain
data.value: Disabling it removes crash reports that help diagnose problems and does not improve performance.

data.name: CheckInputQueuesExplain
data.value: Shrinking MouseDataQueueSize or KeyboardDataQueueSize can drop input during bursts; it does not reduce input lag.

data.name: CheckCsrssPriorityExplain
data.value: csrss.exe is a critical Windows process; forcing its CPU or I/O priority gives no measurable benefit and can cause instability.

data.name: CheckMpoExplain
data.value: OverlayTestMode turns off MPO. Keep it only if it fixes flickering on your GPU; otherwise MPO lowers latency in windowed games.

data.name: CheckMemoryManagementExplain
data.value: DisablePagingExecutive, LargeSystemCache, IoPageLockLimit and CacheUnmapBehindLengthInMB are server-era values that waste memory on desktops.

data.name: CheckRawMouseThrottleExplain
data.value: RawMouseThrottle values only matter for background windows; forcing them changes how high polling-rate mice behave and gives no gain in games.

data.name: CheckGlobalTimerExplain
data.value: Makes every process share the finest timer any app requests, as on Windows 10. It raises power use; keep it only if a specific old game needs it.

data.name: CheckProcessorStateRangeExplain
data.value: A tweaking tool lowered the highest value Windows allows for minimum processor state (normally 100%). The setting stays stuck at that value, the power plan editor cannot raise it and the CPU throttling tweak may fail. The repair puts the Windows limit of 100% back.

data.name: ScriptsDescription
data.value: The author's interactive tools, run exactly as he documents them: TweakHub opens an administrator PowerShell window that downloads the script from tools.mariusheier.com and runs it. TweakHub does not check or change what the script does.

data.name: ScriptCpuDirect
data.value: Maps every USB device to its controller and CPU, then offers to enable MSI and turn off USB power saving.

data.name: ScriptDeepPoll
data.value: Measures the real polling rate and jitter of mouse and controller with kernel tracing.

data.name: ScriptDeepLog
data.value: Records 30 seconds of controller input; it lists what it would send before any upload.

data.name: ScriptRig
data.value: Compares your USB setup with profiles shared by other users and can submit yours.

data.name: ScriptWarningMessage
LoadingUsb
data.value: Tracing USB devices to the CPU…

data.name: LinksDescription
data.value: Checks whether the GPU, NVMe drives, PCIe cards and USB devices run at full width and speed, and what goes through the chipset. Read only: move a device to another slot or port, then press Scan again.

data.name: NoLinkDevices
data.value: No PCIe device with link information was found.

data.name: LinkOk
data.value: Running with every lane and at the full speed it supports.

data.name: LinkOkChipset
data.value: Running with every lane and at full speed. It goes through the chipset, which shares one link to the CPU with USB, SATA and the other devices on it.

data.name: LinkLanesMissing
data.value: Running at x{0} instead of x{1}. Usually the slot is narrower or a nearby M.2 or slot shares its lanes: check the lane-sharing table in the motherboard manual, or move the device to a full-width slot.

data.name: LinkGpuOnChipset
data.value: The GPU goes through the chipset and shares its link to the CPU with USB, SATA and other drives. Move it to the main x16 slot, the one closest to the CPU.

data.name: LinkGpuGenLower
data.value: Link at PCIe {0} instead of {1}. GPUs lower it when idle: open a game or a 3D app and press Scan. If it stays the same, the slot or the CPU is limited to PCIe {0}.

data.name: LinkGenLower
data.value: Link at PCIe {0} instead of {1}: the slot is slower than the device. If the motherboard has a free PCIe {1} slot, move it there.

data.name: LinkHidden
data.value: This card has a PCIe switch on board: Windows only sees the internal link, and the real one cannot be read without data from the GPU driver.

data.name: LinkChipsetUnknown
data.value: Chipset not recognized: the shared bandwidth cannot be calculated.

data.name: LinkChipsetIdle
data.value: No fast device goes through the chipset.

data.name: LinkChipsetOk
data.value: Fast devices on the chipset: {0}, up to {1:0.#} GB/s. The {3} link ({2:0.#} GB/s) is enough.

data.name: LinkChipsetShared
data.value: Fast devices on the chipset: {0}, together up to {1:0.#} GB/s, more than the {3} link to the CPU ({2:0.#} GB/s). Used at the same time, for example copying between two SSDs, they split the bandwidth. This is theoretical bandwidth, not measured traffic.

data.name: LinkUsbSlowPort
data.value: It supports USB 3 but is running at USB 2 (480 Mb/s). Plug it into a USB 3 port (usually blue or marked SS) with a USB 3 cable and no USB 2 hub in between, then press Scan.

data.name: LinkUsbInputHub
data.value: It goes through {0} hub(s). For a mouse or keyboard a port on the PC is better: it does not share the hub with other devices.

data.name: LinkUsbSharedHub
data.value: Shares a hub with {0}: everything behind a hub goes through one link to the PC, so used together they split the bandwidth. Plug one of them straight into the PC.

data.name: LinkUsbOk
data.value: Running at the speed it supports.

data.name: LinkUsbUnknown
data.value: The hub did not report the speed of this port.

data.name: BoardNotListed
data.value: This motherboard is not in TweakHub's list yet: the advice stays generic.

data.name: HintFasterM2
data.value: M.2 slots up to PCIe {0} on this motherboard: {1}.

data.name: HintCpuM2
data.value: M.2 slots wired to the CPU on this motherboard: {0}. At least one looks free: it is the best place for the system or games drive.

data.name: HintSlotGen
data.value: The main slot on this motherboard ({0}) runs up to PCIe {1}.

data.name: LinkSlotLimit
data.value: The slot runs up to PCIe {0}: the device is at the most this motherboard allows.

data.name: LinkSlotLanes
data.value: This motherboard wires the M.2 slot with x{0} lanes: the drive runs at what the slot offers, not at its full speed.

data.name: HintWiderM2
data.value: M.2 slots with x{0} lanes on this motherboard: {1}.
